claims.text: Interest is estimated, not counted: how often the team changes the area, combined with how much extra each change costs because of the debt; debt in a file nobody opens charges almost nothing.

change-hotspots.sh at stage-3 counts the commits that changed each .cs and .dart file under DonHang.* (git log --format= --name-only, then sort | uniq -c), leaves out Migrations/, shows the top 15 by default, and exits with a message on a shallow clone (lines 10-13).
git log --format= --name-only prints, for each commit, the names of the files it changed and no commit header; the pathspec magic ':(glob)' and ':(exclude,glob)' include and exclude paths by glob.
A commit count says nothing about the size of each change, so a hotspot points to where to look rather than measuring interest.

Captured output at stage-3: OrdersController.cs 11 commits, Dtos.cs 8; the 15th line shows 3 commits; api_client.dart also has 3 and is left off by the name tie-break (sort -k2,2); keycloak_sign_in.dart 1; PostgresFixture.cs 2; 169 files counted.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 outputs/stage-3/scripts/management/change-hotspots.txt; git log stage-3 with the script's pathspecs, without head

claims.text: Most commits in the example repository were made to build the course step by step, so the ranking shows how the example grew, not where a team struggled.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang git log up to stage-3; DECISIONS.md section 3, 2026-10-06 outline tech-debt-and-adr point (5)

claims.text: Register at stage-3: N3 is in Dtos.cs and OrdersController.cs, paid on each DTO change, 'Chấp nhận' since removing the field breaks clients on /api/v1, reviewed when /api/v1 gets an end date; N4 is in api_client.dart and keycloak_sign_in.dart, repaid when the app moves to the cluster.

Register lines 10-12 name four decisions: trả ngay, trả cùng lần sửa tới vùng đó, chấp nhận (keep paying, knowing why), xóa sổ (the area is going away). N1 is 'Trả ngay': dump then drop by one migration, about a day; its interest is that each donhang migration asks whether the table is still used.

Repay now when interest is steady and repayment cheap; with the next change when it will touch the same lines anyway; keep paying knowingly when repaying costs more or breaks others; write off when the area is going away. Frequency raises priority but does not decide alone.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 3; register lines 10-12, row N3

claims.text: N1's table is not a file, so it never appears; PostgresFixture.cs, listed beside it, is counted at 2 commits; the migrations that pay N1's interest are excluded by the script's pathspec. For debt in data or configuration the team judges how often it is paid.
claims.source_hint: scripts/management/change-hotspots.sh @ stage-3 lines 22-23 pathspecs; register row N1

claims.text: T1 was repaid in one commit by scripts/k8s/kustomize-config-repo.sh, moving the config repository to Kustomize overlays, checked by what Argo CD reported as different: only the api's ConfigMap and Deployment.
claims.source_hint: tech-debt-register.md line 27 @ stage-3; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/kustomize-config-repo.txt, section 'what Argo CD finds different'

claims.text: Register lines 36-37: repayment time is shown in the plan as its own story or a stated share of a sprint, not hidden in another task's estimate.

Repaying in small verified steps beside feature work keeps the system shippable; a rewrite holds back delivery for its length and ships nothing that can be checked in use until it ends. Opposing view: a rewrite can be right when no sequence of small steps reaches the new shape.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 4, misconception 2; foundation.l1.code-smells-basic outline items 2, 4

claims.text: Debt time hidden inside feature estimates tends to be used by that feature, as hidden padding is, and nobody can see whether the debt was repaid.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 5, misconception 3; management.l2.schedule-buffer summary line 2

claims.text: Treating the register as a portfolio: every item is held for a stated reason and the reasons are compared side by side.

N4's interest is paid only when someone needs the app at another address, and the move to the cluster must deal with those addresses anyway, so repaying with that change is preferable to repaying now.
claims.source_hint: register row N4 (Lãi mỗi lần sửa, Quyết định); hotspot output

claims.text: Migrations/ is left out because EF Core rewrites the model snapshot file in that folder with every migration added, so that file's commit count reflects no one's choice (script comment, lines 16-19).
